title: Sea Level Simulator
subtitle: Interactive global coastal inundation simulation based on SRTM 90m elevation and hydrological modeling.
dataset: CGIAR-CSI SRTM 90m Digital Elevation Database v4.1 & SCALGO Hydrology Engine

hotspots.name: Gulf of Mexico & Mississippi Delta
hotspots.description: Low-lying Mississippi River Delta and Florida Peninsula, among the most vulnerable coastal zones in North America.

hotspots.name: The Netherlands & North Sea
hotspots.description: Dense delta plain with over 26% of land currently situated below sea level, protected by the Delta Works system.

hotspots.name: Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta
hotspots.description: The world's largest river delta, where tens of millions live less than 5 meters above sea level in cyclone-prone wetlands.

hotspots.name: Nile Delta & Alexandria
hotspots.description: Agricultural breadbasket of Egypt, with historical Alexandria and extensive Mediterranean lagoons at extreme flood risk.

hotspots.name: Venice Lagoon & Po Plain
hotspots.description: Historic Venetian archipelago and the flat Po River Valley, vulnerable to regular 'Acqua Alta' tidal surges.

hotspots.name: Tokyo Bay & Kanto Plain
hotspots.description: Megacity metropolis with extensive reclaimed bay land, subterranean infrastructure, and high population density.

hotspots.name: London & Thames Estuary
hotspots.description: Lowland estuary defended by the Thames Barrier, facing heightened tidal surge frequencies as oceans warm.

hotspots.name: New York Harbor & Manhattan
hotspots.description: Dense island topography where subway tunnels, waterfront districts, and Brooklyn shores face severe storm surge exposure.

hotspots.name: Yangtze Delta & Shanghai
hotspots.description: Massive urban sprawl and global shipping hub built upon soft alluvial silt with average elevations under 4 meters.

hotspots.name: Amazon River Delta
hotspots.description: Vast equatorial delta discharging 20% of global river flow into the Atlantic, encircled by tidal mangrove forests.

scenarios.title: Lowered Baseline (-1 m)
scenarios.summary: Simulates lowered global sea levels prior to recent anthropomorphic heating or during cooler glacial fluctuation stages.

scenarios.title: +1 Meter Rise
scenarios.summary: Projected near-term high emission trajectory by 2100. Routine high-tide flooding of sunny streets in Miami, Venice, and Jakarta.

scenarios.title: +5 Meters Rise
scenarios.summary: Triggered by rapid disintegration of West Antarctic marine-terminating ice shelves and accelerated Greenland peripheral ice loss.

scenarios.title: +10 Meters Rise
scenarios.summary: Complete disappearance of southern Florida, large portions of Bangladesh, the Netherlands coastal ring, and Shanghai lowlands.

scenarios.title: +20 Meters Rise
scenarios.summary: Multi-century equilibrium state under sustained elevated atmospheric CO2 levels, submerging lowlands and shifting continental shorelines.

scenarios.title: +60 Meters Rise
scenarios.summary: Catastrophic melting of the entire Antarctic and Greenland ice caps. Complete redrawing of Earth's continental maps.
